helpers.note: DragonFlightHistory::new builds the engine's history from caller-given samples (newest first) for a dragon met mid-flight; vanilla's DragonFlightHistory constructor only fills a fresh ring with zero samples and never takes a list
getter of the engine history's sample list, for callers and tests; vanilla keeps its ring private and exposes only get(delay)
f32 narrowing of simulation::yaw_radians (the release's float degrees-to-radians product, which cites its own sources); vanilla multiplies by the constant inline in EnderDragon and has no such method
the unit box of the moving block's own cell from its engine block position; vanilla writes new AABB(pos) / Shapes.block() inline at each use, and the callers cite the methods they mirror
dispatch on the engine's Mover enum to move_entity (player) or move_body (other entities), both of which are Entity.move and cite it; the split by mover is the engine's own
maps an entity registry name to the engine's RiddenMobKind enum (camel_husk to Camel); a string-to-enum lookup of the bindings, not vanilla code
membership test on the engine's RiddenMobKind for the AbstractHorse subclasses; vanilla dispatches by class (overrides), not by a method that asks this
membership test on the engine's RiddenMobKind for the AbstractNautilus subclasses; vanilla dispatches by class (overrides), not by a method that asks this
constructor of the engine's RiddenMobState with neutral defaults (attribute base from movement_speed, which cites createAttributes); a struct initializer the bindings overwrite, no vanilla method
derives the engine's per-axis scale from dimensions the caller measured in the game, so a recorded box is reproduced; vanilla has no method that infers a scale from a box
unit conversion: float degrees times 0.017453292F widened to f64; vanilla writes this product inline (no method), and the callers cite getRiddenInput
JOML Math.cosFromSin as JOML's Vector3f.rotateY uses it in 1.20.2 - 1.20.4: library code bundled with the game, not a Minecraft method, so it has no Mojang-named counterpart
membership test on the engine's FluidState enum (Water or Waterlogged); vanilla asks fluid.is(FluidTags.WATER) inline, and the engine's waterlogged variant has no vanilla counterpart

the generous box (move swept, then inflated by a block) whose lily pads the engine removes from a world copy before a pre-1.13 boat move; vanilla instead gives the lily pad no collision box, so this pre-pass and its bound are the engine's own
wraps run_vehicle_move (Entity.move, which cites its sources) with the engine's phase-trace emits before and after; tracing plumbing, no logic of its own
maps an entity registry name (old and new spellings) to the engine's MinecartVariant enum; a string-to-enum lookup of the bindings
membership test on the engine's MinecartVariant for the container carts (chest, hopper); vanilla dispatches by class (AbstractMinecartContainer), not by such a method
builder setter of the engine's MinecartRules (level min y and the TNT game rule the caller reads); mirrors no vanilla method, as its comment says

Default impls of engine structs (MinecartState, MinecartOther, TrackIteration): neutral initial values for the bindings to overwrite; TrackIteration's first = true is the field initializer of NewMinecartBehavior.TrackIteration, which has no method to cite
maps a block state's shape property string to the engine's RailShape enum; a string-to-enum lookup over the engine's world snapshot
public entry point: tick_minecarts_among with no items or containers; delegation only
public entry point: tick_minecarts_with with no end gateways; delegation only
public entry point: tick_minecarts of a single cart, returning its tick; delegation only
Scene accessor: mutable reference to the cart being ticked (carts[current]); engine plumbing standing in for vanilla's this
Scene accessor: shared reference to the cart being ticked (carts[current]); engine plumbing standing in for vanilla's this
Scene getter of the release from the engine's MinecartRules, which picks the version branches; vanilla has no release to ask
Scene getter: whether the rules select the improved behaviour (the engine's MinecartBehavior enum standing in for the behavior object AbstractMinecart picks by the minecart_improvements feature)
Scene shorthand for release().at_least, the engine's version comparison; vanilla has no release to compare
copies the shared SimulationState that Entity.move ran on back into the engine's MinecartState (position, motion, flags, box, fall); a conversion between engine types
